proposals.before: His father, Liu Gu, served as an aide to the Chancellor.
proposals.after: His father, Jie, served as an aide to the Chancellor.
proposals.reason: Chinese 父喈 names the father 喈 (Jie); 'Liu Gu' is not in the source and conflicts with the literal rendering Jie.

proposals.before: a cockfight nearly ruined Lu.
proposals.after: A cockfight raised disaster in the state of Lu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 難興魯邦 states that disaster arose in Lu; 'nearly ruined' invents averted ruin the source does not say.

proposals.before: He beat wife or children on the spot for fault—such was his severity.
proposals.after: He beat wife or children on the spot for fault—such was his fairness.
proposals.reason: Chinese 公正 means fairness or impartiality, not severity; the idiomatic close inverts the historian's stated quality.

proposals.before: Eventually permitted, he retired as supernumerary minister with carriage rails before his gate and another million in silver.
proposals.after: Eventually permitted, he retired as supernumerary minister with carriage rails before his gate and another million in cash.
proposals.reason: Chinese 錢百萬 is cash, not silver.

proposals.before: So Ji An died in provincial exile and Dong Zhongshu sank to tutoring a prince.
proposals.after: So Ji An died in Huaiyang and Dong Zhongshu was reduced to chancellor of a feudal lord.
proposals.reason: 汲黯死于淮陽 is death at Huaiyang, not provincial exile; 諸侯之相 is feudal chancellor, not tutoring a prince.

proposals.before: He soon impeached Wang Yun—Wang Cui—Dong Ai and a dozen more.
proposals.after: He soon concurrently served as palace assistant and memorialized the removal of the vice director, the Prince of Dong'an You, along with Wang Cui, Dong Ai, and more than ten others.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents 'Wang Yun' for 東安公繇 (Prince of Dong'an You) and drops 尚書僕射 and 御史中丞.

proposals.before: When Liu Yao struck Luoyang Tun commanded defense as Pacifying Army general.
proposals.after: When Liu Yao struck Luoyang, Tun commanded the defense as General Who Pacifies the Army.
proposals.reason: Fuses the place Luoyang with Tun and omits 假節、都督城守諸軍事.

proposals.before: =Tun courtesy name Changsheng—upright with his father's manner.
proposals.after: Tun, courtesy name Changsheng, was upright with his father's manner.
proposals.reason: Leading '=' is a lemma marker, not part of the sentence.

proposals.before: After Wu fell he shared credit with his brother Yu, who gained a pavilion marquisate.
proposals.after: After Wu was pacified, for He Jiao’s merit in planning counsel his younger brother Yu was granted the rank of Marquis of Runan Pavilion.
proposals.reason: The Chinese 以參謀議功，賜弟郁爵 credits He Jiao’s planning merit and then grants the pavilion marquisate to the younger brother; it does not say the brothers shared the credit.

proposals.before: The younger Xun Kai snubbed Wu Mao’s refusal of his patronizing friendship.
proposals.after: Xun Kai of Yingchuan, younger than Mao and a son of Emperor Wu’s paternal aunt, prided himself on noble kinship, wished to befriend Mao, was refused, and therefore resented him.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence makes Xun Kai ‘snub’ Mao’s refusal and obscures the actual sequence: Kai sought the tie, Mao refused, Kai bore the grudge.

proposals.before: Loyal and blunt, he advised Emperor Wu on everything.
proposals.after: Loyal and upright, he took the altars of the state as his own charge; the emperor prized and favored him and consulted him on most government affairs.
proposals.reason: 忠正 is loyal-upright, not blunt; 以社稷為己任 and 器而昵之, 政事多諮焉 are omitted.

proposals.before: The emperor made Ren Kai heir tutor—blocking Jia’s scheme to exile rivals.
proposals.after: The emperor followed and made him junior tutor to the heir, remaining palace attendant as before; Chong’s plan did not succeed.
proposals.reason: Chinese does not mention exiling rivals; it records 侍中如故 and 充計畫不行.

proposals.before: Favored at court, Jia Chong craved control while Ren Kai moved with He Jiao and Zhang Hua—rival patrons split the faction map.
proposals.after: Favored by the emperor, Jia Chong wished to monopolize fame and power, while Yu Chun, Zhang Hua, Wen Yong, Xiang Xiu, He Jiao and their like all befriended Kai, and Yang Yao, Wang Xun, and Hua Yi were those Chong held dear, so factional cliques flared.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops several named associates present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: The heir feigned muteness in a grass hut so his brother stole the title.
proposals.after: When Hui’s father died and mourning was completed, Hui returned to his village, built a grass hut, and feigned muteness so that Shu obtained the inherited noble rank.
proposals.reason: 恢父終，服闋 is the father’s death and end of mourning, not the father ending mourning.

proposals.before: Late Wei he served Prince Zhao’s chief clerk.
proposals.after: Late in Xianxi he served as chief clerk to Emperor Wen’s minister of state.
proposals.reason: Chinese 咸熙末，為文帝相國主簿 names the Xianxi era and Emperor Wen (文帝), not a ‘Prince Zhao’ and not a vague ‘Late Wei’ only.

proposals.before: Late Xiandi—became Prince Wen’s minister-of-state chief clerk.
proposals.after: Late Xianxi—became Emperor Wen’s minister-of-state chief clerk.
proposals.reason: 咸熙 is the era Xianxi, not ‘Xiandi’; 文帝 is Emperor Wen.

proposals.before: He urged removing Xun Xu—Zhong Hui’s kinsman—from Prince Zhao’s staff during Shu revolt.
proposals.after: When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Guo Yi urged removing Xun Xu—Hui’s nephew (從甥), raised in Hui’s house and then an aide of Emperor Wen—from that staff.
proposals.reason: 從甥 is a specific kinship, 文帝 is Emperor Wen not Prince Zhao, and 少長會家 is omitted.

proposals.before: Touring the provinces with Huangfu Tao he earned promotion to colonel of the gates—Marquis of Linhai.
proposals.after: With Huangfu Tao and Xun Gao he held credentials, toured inspecting customs, and on return was made colonel of the city gates and Marquis of Linhai.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 荀暠 and the credentials/inspection wording present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: He urged retiring Wang Xiang—the emperor honored Wang Xiang and ignored the memo.
proposals.after: He memorialized to dismiss Grand Guardian Wang Xiang for long illness; an edict favored Xiang and shelved Guang’s memorial.
proposals.reason: 太保 is Grand Guardian, not ‘Grand Tutor’, and 廢朝 / 免之 is dismissal for ceasing court, not a generic retirement.

proposals.before: For helping purge Yang Jun he gained a ten-thousand-household marquisate—rich bounty—and titles for kin.
proposals.after: For merit in executing Yang Jun he was enfeoffed Marquis of Xicheng with ten thousand households and ten thousand bolts of silk; his younger brother Feng became Marquis of Pingqing and his elder brother’s son Kui Marquis Within the Pass.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line erases the named brother 逢 and nephew 逵 and their distinct titles.

proposals.before: Court pressure failed—He Pan pleaded sickness.
proposals.after: Minister of Ceremonies Cheng Can and General of the Left Bian Cui urged him to take the post; an inner edict grew stern, but Pan claimed illness and would not rise.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence omits the two named officials 成粲 and 卞粹 who urged him.

proposals.before: First magistrate of Yewang—Yang Hu often visited—Yi sighed: "Uncle Yangzi why must diminish Guo Daye!"
proposals.after: First he was magistrate of Yewang; Yang Hu often visited; Yi sighed: "Why should Uncle Shuzi rank below Guo Daye!"
proposals.reason: 減 here means ‘be inferior to’, not ‘diminish’ as a transitive verb.

proposals.before: petty rulers like Gong Huan exhaust even sages;
proposals.after: Gong and Huan in power were more than even a great sage could endure;
proposals.reason: Gong Huan fuses two legendary ministers named separately as Gong and Huan occupying office, not a single petty ruler.

proposals.before: Wu Gai kept Wei loyalty; Cui Hong praised Xi Shen; Liu Tun courted Wang Mi; He Pan answered Prince Lun—character shows in crisis.
proposals.after: Wu Gai kept Wei-minister resolve; Cui Hong loved Xi Shen's way; Changsheng urged honor for Wang Mi; He Pan obeyed Zhao Lun's order—a gentleman is seen in the crisis.
proposals.reason: The Chinese urges honor for Wang Mi, loves Xi Shen's way, and obeys Zhao Lun's order; Changsheng is the courtesy name used.

proposals.before: Great enterprise not Yang—Yuanbao mocked Jia.
proposals.after: Daye rejected Yang—Yuanbao mocked Jia.
proposals.reason: Parallel with Yuanbao shows Daye is a courtesy name, not the noun great enterprise.

decisions.reason: 父喈 names the father 喈; Liu Gu is not in the Chinese and contradicts the given name Jie.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 父喈

sourceWitness.excerpt: 其公正如此

decisions.reason: 復賜錢百萬 is a further grant of cash, not silver.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 復賜錢百萬

decisions.reason: 汲黯死于淮陽 is death at Huaiyang, not exile; 諸侯之相 is chancellor to a feudal lord, not tutoring a prince.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 尋兼御史中丞，奏免尚書僕射、東安公繇及王粹、董艾等十餘人

decisions.after: When Liu Yao struck Luoyang, Tun was made General Who Pacifies the Army, granted a staff of authority, and put in command of the city’s defenses.
decisions.reason: The original omits 假節 and 都督城守諸軍事; the proposal still omits both appointments and only retitles the generalship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以暾為撫軍將軍、假節、都督城守諸軍事

decisions.reason: The leading “=” is a lemma marker on 暾字長升, not part of the sentence.

sourceWitness.excerpt: =暾字長升

decisions.reason: 以參謀議功 credits He Jiao’s planning; 賜弟郁爵汝南亭侯 grants the pavilion marquisate to the younger brother, not shared credit.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以參謀議功，賜弟郁爵汝南亭侯

decisions.reason: 荀愷欲與茂交，距而不答，由是致怨: Kai sought the tie, Mao refused, and Kai resented him; the original reverses who snubbed whom.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 欲與茂交，距而不答，由是致怨

decisions.reason: 忠正 is loyal and upright, not blunt; the sentence also has 以社稷為己任, 器而昵之, and 政事多諮焉.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 性忠正，以社稷為己任，帝器而昵之，政事多諮焉

decisions.reason: The source records 太子少傅, 侍中如故, and 充計畫不行; it does not mention exiling rivals.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 以為太子少傅，而侍中如故，充計畫不行

decisions.reason: The Chinese names 庾純、張華、溫顒、向秀、和嶠 on Kai’s side and 楊珧、王恂、華廙 on Chong’s; the original drops most of them.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 庾純、張華、溫顒、向秀、和嶠之徒皆與愷善，楊珧、王恂、華廙等充所親敬

decisions.reason: 恢父終，服闋 is the father’s death and the end of mourning; 淑得襲爵 is inheritance, not theft, and the original omits the return home.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 恢父終，服闋，乃還鄉里

decisions.after: Late in Xianxi he served as chief clerk to Emperor Wen, the minister of state.
decisions.reason: 咸熙末 and 文帝 are right against Late Wei and Prince Zhao, but 文帝相國主簿 makes Emperor Wen himself the 相國; “to Emperor Wen’s minister of state” invents a separate chancellor.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 咸熙末，為文帝相國主薄

decisions.reason: 咸熙 is the era Xianxi, not Xiandi; 文帝 is Emperor Wen, not Prince Wen.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 咸熙末，為文帝相國主薄

decisions.after: When Zhong Hui rebelled in Shu, Guo Yi urged removing Xun Xu—Hui’s nephew, raised in Hui’s house and then an aide of Emperor Wen—from that staff.
decisions.reason: 從甥、少長會家, and 文帝掾 must replace kinsman and Prince Zhao, but leaving the characters 從甥 in the idiomatic English is unnatural.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 荀勖即會之從甥，少長會家，勖為文帝掾

decisions.after: With Huangfu Tao and Xun Gao he held credentials, toured inspecting customs, and on return, his report meeting with approval, was transferred to colonel of the city gates and advanced to Marquis of Linhai.
decisions.reason: The proposal rightly restores 荀暠 and 持節循省風俗, but still omits 奏事稱旨 and 進爵, which explain the promotion and the advance in rank.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 與皇甫陶、荀暠持節循省風俗，及還，奏事稱旨，轉城門校尉，進爵臨海侯

decisions.reason: 太保 is Grand Guardian; 奏請免之 after 久疾廢朝 is a request to dismiss, not a generic retirement, and 寢光奏 is shelving the memorial.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太保王祥久疾廢朝，光奏請免之，詔優祥而寢光奏

decisions.reason: The source names 西城侯, 弟逢平卿侯, and 兄子逵關中侯 with 邑萬戶 and 絹萬匹; the original erases those persons and titles.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 封西城侯，邑萬戶，賜絹萬匹，弟逢平卿侯，兄子逵關中侯

decisions.reason: 太常成粲 and 左將軍卞粹 urged him, then 中詔又加切厲; the original omits both named officials.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 太常成粲、左將軍卞粹勸攀蒞職

decisions.reason: 何必減郭大業 means why must Shuzi rank below Daye; diminish as a transitive verb misreads 減, and 叔子 is Shuzi.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 羊叔子何必減郭大業

sourceWitness.excerpt: 共驩在位

decisions.reason: 愛郤詵之道 is loving Xi Shen’s way; 長升勸王彌之尊 urges honor, not courting; 何攀從趙倫之命 is obedience to Zhao Lun’s order.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 崔洪愛郤詵之道，長升勸王彌之尊，何攀從趙倫之命

sourceWitness.excerpt: 大業非楊，元褒誚賈
